legend: This is an interactive problem!

There's a hidden array a1,a2,…,aN$$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_N$$$ of N$$$N$$$ distinct positive integers (where N$$$N$$$ is odd); an incorrect copy of this array is stored in another hidden array b$$$b$$$. Each element of array b$$$b$$$ is defined as follows:
bi=ai−1$$$b_i = a_{i-1}$$$ or bi=ai+1$$$b_i = a_{i+1}$$$ for each i$$$i$$$ where 1<i<N$$$1  \lt  i  \lt  N$$$ (one of the adjacent elements)

You need to determine whether there are two indices i$$$i$$$ and j$$$j$$$ (i≠j$$$i \neq j$$$, 1≤i,j≤N$$$1 \leq i, j \leq N$$$) such that bi=bj$$$b_i = b_j$$$. If such indices exist, return them; otherwise, indicate that no such indices exist.
You can query the elements of arrays a$$$a$$$ and b$$$b$$$ using the following operations:
1 i: returns the value of ai (1≤ai≤109)$$$a_i\ (1 \leq a_i \leq 10^9)$$$
2 i: returns the value of bi (1≤bi≤109)$$$b_i\ (1 \leq b_i \leq 10^9)$$$
You can ask up to a maximum of 20$$$20$$$ queries.
Interaction

First, you must read a line containing a single integer T$$$T$$$ (1≤T≤100$$$1 \leq T \leq 100$$$) denoting the number of test cases. Then follows a description of the interaction for T$$$T$$$ test cases.
For each test case, you must first read a line containing one integer N$$$N$$$ (3≤N≤2 001, N is odd$$$(3 \leq N \leq 2 \ 001,\ N \text{ is odd}$$$).
Then interaction starts. You can print one line, containing:
1 x (Ask about ax$$$a_x$$$): Then, read one line, consisting of one integer, ax$$$a_x$$$.
2 x (Ask about bx$$$b_x$$$): Then, read one line, consisting of one integer, bx$$$b_x$$$.
3 i j (The answer: two indices i$$$i$$$, j$$$j$$$, where bi=bj$$$b_i = b_j$$$ or -1 -1 if there are no such two indices): Then, proceed to the next test if there is any; otherwise, terminate.
After outputting each line, don't forget to flush the output. For example:
fflush(stdout) in C/C++;
System.out.flush() in Java;
sys.stdout.flush() in Python;
flush(output) in Pascal;
See the documentation for other languages.
